4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith]

2:54.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:54.en: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for [all of] you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: [This] worldly life is only amusement and diversion. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and not ask you for your properties

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask you for them and press you, you would withhold, and He would expose your unwillingness

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you "Muslims" before [in former scriptures] and in this [revelation] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast

37:103.en: And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good

37:106.en: Indeed, this was the clear trial

37:107.en: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice

5JuPYyrlxso.speaker: adnan
5JuPYyrlxso.speaker_note: Single voice speaking as the community's imam; uses his own parenting as an example.
5JuPYyrlxso.title: Hajj: Celebration of the Greatest Submission
5JuPYyrlxso.one_line: Allah could have commanded us to do harmful, senseless things but never did; Eid al-Adha celebrates that mercy and Ibrahim's total submission.
5JuPYyrlxso.summary: Given the week before Eid al-Adha, this khutbah starts from 4:66: had Allah ordered people to kill themselves or leave their homes, few would have obeyed. The sheikh shows that Allah once did give such a command, when the Israelites repented from the golden calf by killing one another, to teach that every other command was for their own good. Surah Muhammad makes the same point about wealth: He asks for 2.5% of stagnant wealth, not all of it. Allah's commands are reasoned and serve our interest, and He adds reward on top, like a loving parent who rewards a child for studying. Then the centrepiece: Ibrahim, the man who questioned everything, receives a command with no visible wisdom and asks nothing. Ismail, a teenager, agrees, Shaytan is stoned three times, and the moment both submit coins the word Muslim. Eid celebrates that Allah never asked this of us. So he challenges those who complain about hijab, alcohol or other limits, and ties submission to standing for justice. In the second khutbah he calls this complaining vanity, as if we were speaking to an equal.

outline.heading: Opening
Had We decreed that they kill themselves
outline.gist: An-Nisa 4:66 states a fact the Quran and the Prophet repeat often: Allah never commanded what harms us, and this season is the time to understand it.

outline.heading: The golden calf and the one useless command
outline.gist: To repent from the calf, the Israelites were ordered to draw swords on one another; Musa begged for the decree to be lifted, and Allah forgave them and brought them back. The lesson: I could have made all My commands like this one, but I didn't.

outline.heading: He did not ask for all your wealth
outline.gist: Surah Muhammad: asking for everything would expose our stinginess, so He asked only for 2.5% of stagnant wealth held for a year. He could have, but He didn't.

outline.heading: Commands reasoned for our interest, with reward added
outline.gist: Every command in the deen has a reason aimed at the creation's best interest. No one obliges Allah to make it so; He chose it, and then added reward on top.

outline.heading: The parent who rewards a child for studying
outline.gist: A parent rewards a child for memorizing Quran and studying, though it benefits only the child, because love aligns the child's interest with reward. Some fathers bluff the opposite, but the goal is the same.

outline.heading: No excuse left: ease, not hardship
outline.gist: Allah treats us the same way, so what argument is left for not following His commands? He wants ease, not hardship, and placed no difficulty in the deen (2:185, 22:78).

outline.heading: Ibrahim's long-awaited son, left far away
outline.gist: Allah could have commanded anything, and these days exist because He didn't. Ibrahim waited many years for a son, left him in a barren valley and visited only by permission, until the boy grew old enough to be useful to him.

outline.heading: The vision that kept returning
outline.gist: Ibrahim sees himself slaughtering his son and wakes terrified, not of the dream but that it may be revelation. He gives it time, and the same vision returns every night, down to the place, until he knows it is a command.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner
outline.gist: Throughout the Quran Ibrahim argues with his father, his people, the star-worshippers and the king, and even asks Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead (2:260), so that his heart may be at rest.

outline.heading: No question this time, and a son's consent
outline.gist: This time he asks nothing. He tells his son of the vision and asks his view, and the boy, old enough to understand it as revelation, tells him to do as commanded (37:102).

outline.heading: When they both submitted: the word Muslim is coined
outline.gist: The next verse says 'when they both submitted' (37:103); he presents this as the moment the name Muslim was coined, because both fully submitted to a command whose wisdom they could not see.

outline.heading: Shaytan's three attempts
outline.gist: On the way to Mina Shaytan tries Ibrahim, then the 13-year-old Ismail, then Hajar; each drives him off with seven pebbles. In the Quran's eyes a 13-year-old is accountable and capable of carrying the deen, whatever the world says.

outline.heading: Held down, and the knife that would not cut
outline.gist: Ismail asks to be tied down face away so his father does not falter. Ibrahim sharpens the knife and strikes, with no bluff at any step; the knife does not cut, and some narrations say he tried again.

outline.heading: The call and the great ransom
outline.gist: A voice tells Ibrahim he has fulfilled the vision; this was the clear trial, and Allah ransomed Ismail with a great sacrifice, having no interest in his blood (37:104-107). So we spend these days magnifying and glorifying Allah.

outline.heading: Why we celebrate, and why we should not complain
outline.gist: Eid celebrates that Allah never gave us a senseless command. Complaining about hijab, girlfriends or alcohol is audacity toward the One who set safety barriers out of care; we sacrifice and feed the poor to remind ourselves.

outline.heading: Submission includes standing for justice
outline.gist: The same purposeful commands tell us to stand for justice and speak against oppression. Turning a blind eye to others' suffering ultimately harms ourselves.

outline.heading: Interlude
We have grown vain
outline.gist: Arguing with Allah that a command was not helpful treats Him as a peer. It is only His compassion that made every command benefit us, with reward on top, and that should humble us.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The wisdom and purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah's commands are reasoned and aimed at our best interest by His own choice; He proves it by contrast with the one useless command given to the Israelites, and He rewards obedience on top.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger: religious adherence
themes.note: Ibrahim and Ismail model full submission to a command whose wisdom they could not see; that moment is when the word Muslim was coined, and it leaves us no argument for disobeying commands that plainly help us.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Musa and the repentance of the Israelites after the golden calf, told as Allah's lesson that His commands were otherwise all for their benefit.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: A detailed retelling of Ibrahim's vision, his character as a critical thinker who even asked to see resurrection, Ismail's maturity and consent, and Shaytan's three failed attempts.

themes.label: Hajj, Umrah and Arafah
themes.note: The days of Dhul Hijjah and Eid al-Adha are spent in takbir and sacrifice to celebrate that Allah never commanded anything senseless; the stoning rite recalls the rejection of Shaytan.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Questioning Allah's commands as if negotiating with an equal is vanity; the fact that every command benefits us should humble us.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Commands to stand for justice and speak against oppression also serve us; turning a blind eye to others' suffering ultimately harms ourselves.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: A 13-year-old is accountable and capable of carrying the deen in the Quran's eyes, whatever the world says about being a kid.

stories.point: Allah gave them a command that only harmed them, then lifted it and revived them, so they would realise all His other commands were for their good.

stories.who: Ibrahim and Ismail at Mina

stories.who: Shaytan's three attempts on Ibrahim, Ismail and Hajar
stories.point: All three refused him and stoned him; even a 13-year-old understood and held to Allah's command.

contemporary: Young people's complaints about hijab, alcohol and not having girlfriends

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein [by entering the state of ihram], there is [to be for him] no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do - Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs 'umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allah is appreciative and Knowing

pOjppZHpO88.speaker: adnan
pOjppZHpO88.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Sunday class; mentions living in Mecca for years and doing Hajj with his father
pOjppZHpO88.title: Hajj: Pillars, Obligations and Sunnahs
pOjppZHpO88.one_line: A practical fiqh walk-through of Hajj: the four pillars, the obligatory acts and their expiation, the sunnahs, ihram rules and the sites.
pOjppZHpO88.summary: This class is the technical half of a two-part Hajj series. The sheikh separates three tiers of actions. The four pillars (ihram, standing at Arafah, tawaf al-ifadah and sa'i) can never be substituted; missing one voids the Hajj, and two of them are bound by time, so a pilgrim who misses Arafah must return another year. The obligatory acts (ihram from the miqat, Muzdalifah, stoning, the farewell tawaf, shaving or cutting the hair, the nights at Mina, staying at Arafah until sunset) do not void Hajj if missed, but require a sacrificial animal, and several missed obligations still cost a single animal per person. Sunnahs cost nothing if missed. He chooses the safest combination of opinions, following the modern Saudi Hajj council, and urges flexibility given three million pilgrims: make the intention for raml, the two rakat behind Maqam Ibrahim or touching the Black Stone rather than endangering anyone. He explains ihram dress for men and women, the three prohibitions of Hajj (sexual expression, sin, argument), talbiyah, tawaf and sa'i mechanics, the boundaries of Arafah, and the count of seventy pebbles. He warns against selfies, idle chatter, bad behaviour in Mina and littering in Muzdalifah, and promises the spiritual meanings next week.

outline.heading: Pillars cannot be substituted: the man who skipped sa'i
outline.gist: A missed pillar must be performed itself; a pilgrim who forgot sa'i was told he remained in ihram until he completed it.

outline.heading: The four pillars and the three tawafs
outline.gist: Memorise the four pillars, two bound by time; of the arrival, ifadah and farewell tawafs, whichever you perform first counts as the pillar.

outline.heading: Standing at Arafah and its time window
outline.gist: Any moment at Arafah from the ninth day until before Fajr of the tenth suffices; arriving after that means the Hajj is lost.

outline.heading: Obligation: entering ihram at the miqat
outline.gist: Each region has a miqat; the word joins time and place, and ihram must be entered there, except for those already in Mecca for tamattu'.

outline.heading: The safest combination of opinions for millions
outline.gist: Saudi Hajj teaching moved from one harsh school to a council drawing on all madhhabs; with three million pilgrims, open-mindedness is needed.

outline.heading: One sacrifice for missed obligations
outline.gist: Missing obligations of the same kind costs one animal, not one each; unlike salah, an obligation left even deliberately does not void Hajj.

outline.heading: Obligation: spending the night at Muzdalifah
outline.gist: For most scholars the night at Muzdalifah is obligatory; several such lapses still mean one animal.

outline.heading: Obligation: stoning the jamarat, and deputising
outline.gist: Elderly and frail pilgrims can have someone throw on their behalf; he recalls clinging to his father's belt at the jamarat.

outline.heading: Obligation: the farewell tawaf
outline.gist: Most scholars hold the farewell tawaf obligatory; his teacher advised every pilgrim to offer an animal anyway for unnoticed mistakes.

outline.heading: Obligation: shaving or cutting the hair
outline.gist: Tahallul releases the pilgrim from the sacred state; a minority treat it as a fifth pillar.

outline.heading: Obligation: nights at Mina
outline.gist: Two or three nights at Mina on the 11th to 13th; residents of Mecca may sleep at home.

outline.heading: Obligation: staying at Arafah until sunset
outline.gist: Arafah itself is a pillar, but remaining through the day until sunset is an obligation.

outline.heading: One animal per pilgrim, not per family
outline.gist: Even someone who misses all seven obligations owes one animal, but each spouse owes their own; knowing this is for emergencies, not for planning to skip.

outline.heading: Sunnah: bathing and perfuming before ihram
outline.gist: Sunnahs cost nothing if missed; perfume the body before ihram; showering is allowed in ihram but no scent or accessories.

outline.heading: Sunnah: talbiyah and the arrival tawaf
outline.gist: Talbiyah and the arrival tawaf are agreed sunnahs, with related sunnahs of tawaf to follow.

outline.heading: Sunnah: idtiba and raml in the first three circuits
outline.gist: Men bare the right shoulder and jog lightly, as the Companions did to show the Quraysh their strength; in crowds, the intention suffices.

outline.heading: Sunnah: two rakat behind Maqam Ibrahim
outline.gist: Almost impossible today; pray them anywhere in the Haram with the intention.

outline.heading: Ignorance that endangers lives
outline.gist: Lack of preparation makes people fight for sunnahs, and stampedes killed pilgrims for decades; never endanger anyone for a sunnah.

outline.heading: Sunnah: Zamzam and the Black Stone
outline.gist: Drink Zamzam with dua; if you cannot touch the Black Stone, gesture toward it with intention.

outline.heading: Ask the scholars on site and follow them
outline.gist: Do not plan to skip obligations; if anxious, ask the scholars available at Hajj and follow their answer.

outline.heading: Women's ihram
outline.gist: Women dress modestly in normal clothing without face or hand covering or accessories; national colours help lost elderly women be identified.

outline.heading: Men's ihram and footwear
outline.gist: Two unsewn sheets; sandals that leave the top of the foot and ankles uncovered; a lapse costs an animal, not the Hajj.

outline.heading: Prohibition: no sexual expression in Hajj
outline.gist: Intercourse invalidates Hajj and requires a repeat and a sacrifice, and even a marriage contract in ihram is invalid.

outline.heading: Prohibition: no sinning
outline.gist: Women do not veil their faces because Hajj demands that everyone keep pure ethics; no deviation in honesty, trust or kindness.

outline.heading: Prohibition: no argument
outline.gist: Among people of every culture and exhausted, arguing will ruin your Hajj; he advises a sacrifice if you argued.

outline.heading: Talbiyah: forms and when it ends
outline.gist: Any narrated form is fine; it stops on entering the Haram because you have arrived; men raise their voices, women do not.

outline.heading: Tawaf: the corners and Hijr Ismail
outline.gist: Start at the Black Stone line with takbir without stopping; Hijr Ismail is part of the Ka'bah, where voluntary prayer is allowed.

outline.heading: Wudu for tawaf in the crowds
outline.gist: Most scholars require wudu, but late in a long crowded tawaf he would take Abu Hanifah's view rather than start again.

outline.heading: Sa'i between Safa and Marwa
outline.gist: Seven lengths starting at Safa and ending at Marwa, jogging between the green lights as Hajar did; it can be delayed if exhausted.

outline.heading: Without its symbolism Hajj is just rocks; no selfies
outline.gist: Rituals are empty without understanding; avoid selfies and overuse of technology.

outline.heading: Dua on Safa and Marwa
outline.gist: Climb toward the mountain, face the Ka'bah, say takbir and make dua as the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Fill tawaf and sa'i with Quran and dua, not complaints
outline.gist: Fatigue tempts people to grumble about others; no fixed words are required, just Quran, dua and dhikr; wheelchairs help the elderly.

outline.heading: The map: Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafah
outline.gist: Distances between the sites and the journey from the Haram to Arafah on the ninth.

outline.heading: The pilgrim who stood outside Arafah
outline.gist: A man stayed all day just outside the boundary because it was quieter, and his Hajj was lost; Jabal al-Rahmah and the Farewell Sermon.

outline.heading: Dua at Arafah and the walk to Muzdalifah
outline.gist: Focus on dua and repentance at Arafah, then walk to Muzdalifah, combine Maghrib and Isha and sleep there.

outline.heading: The jamarat: sequence and seventy pebbles
outline.gist: Jamrat al-Aqabah on the tenth with seven pebbles, then all three daily on the 11th to 13th, totalling seventy; combining days is acceptable.

outline.heading: Only pebbles, thrown as a ritual
outline.gist: Shoes and other objects are not allowed; pebbles from Muzdalifah are plentiful.

outline.heading: The trend of skipping Mina
outline.gist: Some plan to sleep in hotels and pay the animal; planning to omit obligations makes acceptance far less likely.

outline.heading: Bad behaviour in Mina after tahallul
outline.gist: Cards and shisha in Mina; you are still a guest of Allah and must act like one.

outline.heading: Throwing at the jamarat with care
outline.gist: The pillars mark where Ibrahim was confronted by Shaytan; throw gently one by one, not aiming to hit anyone.

outline.heading: Do not litter Muzdalifah
outline.gist: Muzdalifah is a sacred site that turns into a dump; leave nothing behind.

outline.heading: Outro

wPyQLw_eEFM.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 5
wPyQLw_eEFM.one_line: Self-honesty through life's milestones, the examples of the Prophet, Ayyub and Ka'b ibn Malik, and why honest striving needs balance.
wPyQLw_eEFM.summary: He likens honesty to an ointment that stings on a burn but heals, while self-deception soothes like water until the limb is lost. The third method of self-honesty is to walk through your life's milestones, the moments of testing that arrive without dramatic music, noticing what you have selectively forgotten and why. Facing that clutter is what lets a person be comfortable in his own company, unlike those who flee solitude into drink, drugs and screens. The Prophet, despite orphanhood and poverty, was at peace with himself, could spend weeks alone in reflection, understood people without idolising or dismissing them, and showed disappointment only to help others see their own faults. Ayyub, stripped of everything, was too honest about his long years of blessing to ask for relief, saying only that harm had touched him and Allah is the Most Merciful. Ka'b ibn Malik, a poet skilled at crafting narratives, refused to invent an excuse for missing Tabuk and accepted fifty days of boycott and a tempting offer from a foreign king. Self-honesty means being a detective who suspects everything and welcomes feedback as a gift. But honesty also reveals how far one is from the ideal, which can provoke excess, so the Prophet constantly brought companions like Abu al-Darda, Abdullah ibn Amr and Hanzalah back to balance; this, he argues, is what bid'ah truly guards against.

outline.heading: Honesty is an ointment on a burn
outline.gist: It stings but heals; self-deception soothes like water until the limb must be amputated.

outline.heading: Third method: walk through your milestones
outline.gist: Most of life runs on autopilot; a few defining highs and lows are where Allah watches closely.

outline.heading: Defining moments come without music
outline.gist: Unlike films, life gives no signal; self-honesty helps you recognise testing moments past, present and future.

outline.heading: Selective forgetting
outline.gist: Combing your timeline takes a week and uncovers chapters the mind set aside; ask why.

outline.heading: Write your own biography
outline.gist: Detail the tests you passed and failed; even all failures can be redeemed by a true tawbah.

outline.heading: Do it yourself
outline.gist: Start around age ten, year by year; you can do for free what a therapist would charge for.

outline.heading: Why you avoid parts of your life
outline.gist: The answers are gold; covering clutter with a blanket works until the room has no space left.

outline.heading: Unresolved issues ruin intimate company
outline.gist: Friends and spouses with unresolved issues cannot enjoy time alone together; the same is true with yourself.

outline.heading: Fleeing yourself into distraction
outline.gist: Drink, drugs and television ease the discomfort of being left with oneself.

outline.heading: The Prophet was at ease with himself
outline.gist: Spending weeks alone in reflection at forty is only possible for one with inner peace.

outline.heading: Peace despite childhood hardship
outline.gist: Orphaned, unschooled and working as a shepherd, he still grew up with clarity and honesty about himself.

outline.heading: Know yourself to understand others
outline.gist: Without self-knowledge people either idolise or cancel others; do not try to please the masses.

outline.heading: The Prophet's disappointment as teaching
outline.gist: His smile of displeasure aimed to make people disappointed in themselves so they would learn.

outline.heading: Ayyub too honest to ask for ease
outline.gist: He was embarrassed to ask for relief until his years of hardship matched his decades of blessing.

outline.heading: Ayyub's dua without a request
outline.gist: After his wife sold her hair to feed him, he said only that harm had touched him and Allah is the Most Merciful.

outline.heading: He never asked for anything back
outline.gist: Allah restored all he lost, yet he never requested it; he saw asking to remove a trial as objecting to it.

outline.heading: Ka'b ibn Malik delays and misses Tabuk
outline.gist: He told the story himself in a long narration; meaning to follow the army, he put it off until too late.

outline.heading: The urge to construct a narrative
outline.gist: Seeing only the disabled and hypocrites left in Madinah, he faced the human pull to justify himself, though he was a poet by trade.

outline.heading: Watching others lie and succeed
outline.gist: Those ahead of him gave false excuses, received the Prophet's prayer and left unshamed, and he nearly caved.

outline.heading: Ka'b tells the truth
outline.gist: He admitted he could argue his way out with anyone but had no excuse, and the Prophet said this one has spoken truly.

outline.heading: Two slaps in a row
outline.gist: Self-honesty hurts once in facing the truth and again in bearing the consequences: fifty days of boycott.

outline.heading: Nearly recanting under pressure
outline.gist: People urged him to retract and offer an excuse; a famous man risks more by being honest.

outline.heading: The foreign king's letter
outline.gist: A northern king invited him over with a royal letter; recognising a test, he burnt it.

outline.heading: Be a detective who suspects everything
outline.gist: Like a good detective, suspect even your own beliefs and deeds to find the lies in your narrative.

outline.heading: Feedback becomes a gift
outline.gist: One searching for the truth thanks those who point out his flaws; offence comes from caring about the facade.

outline.heading: Neither true nor false feedback can hurt you
outline.gist: True criticism is useful information; false criticism cannot touch someone who knows himself.

outline.heading: Abu al-Darda and Salman
outline.gist: Abu al-Darda's devotion led him to neglect his wife; Salman corrected him and the Prophet confirmed that body, soul and family have rights.

outline.heading: The three who vowed extreme worship
outline.gist: The Prophet told them his sunnah of praying and sleeping, fasting and eating, and marrying was the model.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Amr and the Quran
outline.gist: He bargained down to completing it every three days and later regretted not keeping the Prophet's easier advice.

outline.heading: Hanzalah fears hypocrisy
outline.gist: Feeling spiritual heights with the Prophet and ordinary life at home, he was told there is an hour for this and an hour for that.

outline.heading: The Prophet's job was bringing people back
outline.gist: He moderated honest people's excess; today scholars beg people just to pray.

outline.heading: What bid'ah really guards against
outline.gist: It names exaggerated responses that destroy functionality, like monastic celibacy; the Prophet always kept his roles and simple joys.

outline.heading: Strive to resemble him, not exceed him
outline.gist: Honesty shows Jannah is beyond any price, but the answer is to follow the Prophet closely, not to do more.

outline.heading: An honest community needs regulators, not beggars
outline.gist: Begging people to give time and wealth cheapens the call; leaders should only need to keep people from going overboard.

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" Allah said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful

7:22.ar: فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورࣲۚ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمۡ أَنۡهَكُمَا عَن تِلۡكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
7:22.en: So he made them fall, through deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

DvS9e2Z_yV4.speaker: adnan
DvS9e2Z_yV4.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan continues his own Hajj series from the previous week's fiqh session; mentions living in Mecca
DvS9e2Z_yV4.title: The Spirituality of Hajj, Part 1
DvS9e2Z_yV4.one_line: Hajj read through three parallel stories, beginning with Adam and Eve: their fall, repentance at Arafah, planning at Muzdalifah, defeating Shaytan at Mina and building the first House.
DvS9e2Z_yV4.summary: After a week on the rulings of Hajj, the sheikh turns to its meaning: without the symbolism, the pilgrim travels across the world to walk around rocks. He proposes three parallel lines to reflect on during Hajj: Adam and Eve, Ibrahim and his family, and the Prophet and his Companions, plus the pilgrim's own. Most of the night goes to Adam and Eve. Placed in a safe garden, Adam resented being a servant who would die; Shaytan exploited his fear and greed, the two drives of the nafs. Sent down, the couple parted at Safa and Marwa and wandered for years, learning to value what they lost. They reunited at Arafah, where knowledge turned into real understanding (ma'rifah) and the first repentance occurred, and where Allah drew all their descendants out and took the covenant. Muzdalifah is drawing close and planning; Mina is resolve and hope; at al-Aqabah Adam stoned Shaytan; then he built the Ka'bah as a home for all of Allah's servants. Pilgrims stand equally as children of the same parents. He adds the tragedy of Qabil and Habil, the gift of Shith who taught the shared ethics found in every religion, and begins Ibrahim's line with Hajar left in the valley, trusting that Allah commanded it.

outline.heading: Every act of worship has an outer form and an inner meaning
outline.gist: Last week's rulings tell you what to do; without the purpose behind the movements, worship like salah feels awkward.

outline.heading: Without its meaning, Hajj is just rocks and sand
outline.gist: Leaving a green country to walk around stones makes no sense unless you understand why you are there.

outline.heading: Once in a lifetime is enough
outline.gist: Hajj understood properly changes a life; repeating it takes places from Muslims who will never get to go.

outline.heading: The Arabs knew Hajj but corrupted it
outline.gist: Ibrahim's descendants kept the rite but filled it with idolatrous practice, which the Prophet cleansed.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's call and the promise that people will come
outline.gist: People arrive on foot and on lean camels from every distant land, to witness benefits, remember Allah and feed the poor.

outline.heading: Three parallel lines of reflection
outline.gist: Adam and Eve, Ibrahim's family, and the Prophet with his Companions; keep at least one clearly in mind during Hajj.

outline.heading: Why the Adam story at Mecca was common knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran corrects common knowledge only when it is wrong; the Prophet refined rather than replaced what the Arabs knew.

outline.heading: Adam's garden was a safe place, not the final Paradise
outline.gist: He holds the view that the garden was a protected place where Adam would not hunger or be exposed, since no one is expelled from the eternal Paradise.

outline.heading: Resenting servanthood and death
outline.gist: Adam disliked being a servant who would die; Shaytan offered kingship and immortality, but servanthood to Allah means serving people and the world.

outline.heading: The angels' question and Adam's capacity to learn
outline.gist: Allah taught Adam the names and showed the angels a creature with a remarkable intellect; nature outside the garden is brutal.

outline.heading: Fear and greed: the nafs in a nutshell
outline.gist: Adam could not yet control his fear of death and his wish for more, the two drives that make people do foolish things.

outline.heading: The first sin was destined: Musa argues with Adam
outline.gist: Musa blames Adam on the Day of Judgment and Adam wins the argument; Adam was destined for earth before he was created.

outline.heading: Their weaknesses exposed
outline.gist: Their nakedness symbolised every inner weakness laid bare: greed, fear, arrogance, vanity, laziness.

outline.heading: No one has lost more than Adam
outline.gist: Taught directly by Allah and given every security, he lost it all with no way back in his lifetime.

outline.heading: Parting at Safa and Marwa
outline.gist: The stories say Adam came down on Safa and Eve on Marwa, too ashamed to speak, and walked off in different directions.

outline.heading: Years lost: learning to value blessings
outline.gist: Most people only appreciate what they had once it is gone; losing each other was worse than losing the garden.

outline.heading: Reunited at Arafah
outline.gist: Adam saw Eve from the mount and they recognised each other, the root of the name Arafah.

outline.heading: Information versus true understanding (ilm and ma'rifah)
outline.gist: Adam had been taught but did not yet understand; real comprehension came only after loss.

outline.heading: Being a servant is the best description of you
outline.gist: They grasped they must control their whims and that servanthood and stewardship are the greatest honours; losing one thing need not mean throwing away everything.

outline.heading: The first repentance in human history
outline.gist: Allah gave Adam words to say: we have wronged ourselves; owning the wrong without blaming Allah is the key, and we stand where they stood to do the same.

outline.heading: Standing at Arafah in daylight
outline.gist: The standing is in daylight because it is a time of enlightenment, and the long walk to Muzdalifah marks the gap between understanding and action.

outline.heading: The covenant of Adam's descendants
outline.gist: At Arafah Allah brought out all of Adam's children and they testified that He is their Lord.

outline.heading: The part of you that always knows its Lord
outline.gist: Beneath the noise of the nafs, everyone carries something that calls them back to Allah, so no one can claim they never knew.

outline.heading: Adam the first khalifa
outline.gist: Ibn Abbas says Adam understood his purpose as servant and steward; the first revealed use of the word khalifa was for Dawud.

outline.heading: Dawud's forty years and the fear of death
outline.gist: Adam gave Dawud forty years of his life, then nearly took them back; Islam asks us to accept death, not to enjoy it.

outline.heading: All equally children of Adam and Eve
outline.gist: Simple ihram clothing shows that no race, wealth or age gives anyone a greater claim to the parents who stood there.

outline.heading: Muzdalifah: drawing close and making a plan
outline.gist: From zulfa, nearness; the couple planned their family and their resistance to Shaytan, so pilgrims gather pebbles in preparation.

outline.heading: Why Arafah lies outside the Haram
outline.gist: An early scholar asked his teacher this before Hajj; the answer: the Haram is Allah's courtyard and Arafah His door, where servants wait until He lets them in.

outline.heading: Mina: the place of hopes and resolve
outline.gist: Every prophet performed Hajj; at Mina Adam and Eve resolved to earn their way back to the garden, while Shaytan watched his victory unravel.

outline.heading: Al-Aqabah: Adam stones Shaytan
outline.gist: Shaytan confronted Adam at the obstacle and Adam drove him off with pebbles; then came the first sacrifice.

outline.heading: Adam builds the first House
outline.gist: Commanded to build, Adam laid the Ka'bah and circled it; it was later lost and revived by Nuh and then Ibrahim.

outline.heading: Prophets who passed through these valleys
outline.gist: Seventy prophets prayed at Masjid al-Khayf, and the Prophet named valleys where he could almost see Musa and Yunus passing in pilgrimage.

outline.heading: Bayt means home and family
outline.gist: Allah needs no house; we do. Nuh's prayer for whoever enters his house means his family; the Ka'bah is a home for all of Allah's servants.

outline.heading: Why we face the House in every prayer
outline.gist: Each takbir toward the Ka'bah keeps alive the story of when our parents understood their purpose.

outline.heading: Your own line: what will you realise and change?
outline.gist: Beyond reflecting on humanity as one family, ask what you will understand at Arafah, plan at Muzdalifah and throw away at Mina.

outline.heading: Mecca's beauty is history, not scenery
outline.gist: Like children fighting over an ugly family house, the value is sentimental: this is where our parents began the story.

outline.heading: The Ka'bah as the first family home
outline.gist: Building a bayt made them a family; Hajj celebrates humanity under Allah's care and the value of figuring things out for yourself.

outline.heading: Qabil, Habil and the gift of Shith
outline.gist: Stories place the murder of Habil near Mina, the worst grief of Adam and Eve, followed by the glad news of Shith, given fifty scriptures.

outline.heading: Shared ethics in every religion
outline.gist: All faiths teach honesty, trust and that ends do not justify means, against philosophies of playing dirty; he traces this to Shith's teaching.

outline.heading: Adam's death at Abu Qubays
outline.gist: Adam died at the foot of Abu Qubays by Safa, at peace that Shith had inherited his realisations; the place of the graves is uncertain.

outline.heading: Summing up the line of Adam and Eve
outline.gist: Hajj is returning to the place where our parents learned, repented and built the first home.

outline.heading: The lines progress from two people to the whole ummah
outline.gist: Adam and Eve, then Ibrahim's family of three, then the Prophet's community; the themes of unity and repentance reveal themselves to anyone who lives them.

outline.heading: Ibrahim, Sarah and Hajar
outline.gist: Sarah's pain at Hajar's son led Ibrahim to separate them; Allah sent them much farther than he planned.

outline.heading: The journey south to a forgotten sacred place
outline.gist: Ibrahim had travelled from Iraq to Egypt but never south; the Ka'bah's site had been lost and some thought it was in Jerusalem.

outline.heading: Leaving his family in a barren valley
outline.gist: Ibrahim's prayer shows he knew the site of the Sacred House before it was rebuilt; this was the first of two partings from Isma'il.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner who never questioned a command
outline.gist: He argued with his people, the king and even asked how Allah revives the dead, yet obeyed a direct command without question.

outline.heading: Hajar: is it Allah who commanded this?
outline.gist: When he nodded, she accepted that Allah would not abandon them; Ibrahim's line of Hajj begins here.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Hajj, Umrah and Arafah
themes.note: The rites of Hajj as a re-enactment of the stories of Adam and Eve and of Ibrahim's family.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Adam's fall, repentance, covenant, building the Ka'bah and death, with Dawud and Shith.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: The first repentance at Arafah: owning the wrong without blaming Allah.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Fear and greed as the drives of the nafs that Shaytan exploits, and the inner weaknesses the fall exposed.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Servanthood and stewardship as the best description of the human being.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Most people only value blessings after losing them; the wise value them now.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: All pilgrims are equally children of Adam and Eve, shown in the simple ihram.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him

quran.point: Ibrahim's call to Hajj and the promise that people will come from every far land.
In the garden Adam would not go hungry, unclothed, thirsty or exposed to the sun.
Shaytan offers Adam the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays.
Allah announces a khalifa on earth and the angels question it.
Allah taught Adam the names.
Their nakedness was exposed after eating, symbolising inner weaknesses.
Adam received words from his Lord and was forgiven.
We have wronged ourselves: the first repentance.
The covenant taken from Adam's descendants.
Dawud made a khalifa, the first revealed use of the word.
Whoever enters my house means whoever joins my family.
Ibrahim settles his family in an uncultivated valley by the Sacred House.
Ibrahim asks to be shown how Allah gives life to the dead.

hadith.gist: Musa argues with Adam over the sin that removed people from the garden, and Adam wins by pointing out it was written before he was created.
At Na'man near Arafah Allah brought forth Adam's descendants and took the covenant from them.
Adam saw the light between Dawud's eyes, gave him forty of his years, and later at death nearly reclaimed them.
Seventy prophets prayed at Masjid al-Khayf; the Prophet named valleys and described earlier prophets passing through them on pilgrimage.
Of the scriptures sent to humanity, fifty were given to Shith.

maxims: Without the symbolism, Hajj is just rocks and sand
Being a servant is the best description of you
Information is not understanding
We did this to ourselves: the key to repentance
Allah does not need a house; you do
No one is more a child of Adam than anyone else

stories.who: Adam and Eve's fall, separation and reunion
stories.point: Fear and greed led to loss; years apart taught them what they had, and understanding led to repentance at Arafah.

stories.who: Musa arguing with Adam on the Day of Judgment
stories.point: The first sin was destined; Adam was always meant for earth.

stories.who: Adam giving Dawud forty years
stories.point: Fear of death never fully leaves; accept it.

stories.who: An early scholar asking why Arafah is outside the Haram
stories.point: Arafah is Allah's door and the Haram His courtyard: servants wait at the door, then are admitted.

stories.who: Qabil, Habil and the birth of Shith
stories.point: Grief was followed by a son who taught humanity its basic ethics.

stories.who: Ibrahim leaving Hajar and Isma'il in the valley
stories.point: A questioning mind still submits to a clear command; Hajar trusts that Allah will not abandon them.

takeaways: Go to Hajj with at least one of the three lines of reflection clear in your mind
At Arafah, own your mistakes without blaming anyone and repent as Adam did
Use Muzdalifah and Mina to plan concrete changes and throw away specific vices
Value your blessings now rather than after losing them
Perform Hajj once and leave space for Muslims who have never been

71:1.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ أَنۡ أَنذِرۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
71:1.en: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment

71:2.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
71:2.en: He said, "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner

71:3.en: [Saying], 'Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me

71:4.ar: يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمۡ وَيُؤَخِّرۡكُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۚ إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا جَآءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُۚ لَوۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
71:4.en: Allah will forgive you of your sins and delay you for a specified term. Indeed, the time [set by] Allah, when it comes, will not be delayed, if you only knew

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said, "My Lord, indeed I invited my people [to truth] night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But my invitation increased them not except in flight

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And indeed, every time I invited them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with [great] arrogance

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: Then I announced to them and [also] confided to them secretly

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver

71:11.en: He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers

71:13.ar: مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارࣰ ا
71:13.en: What is [the matter] with you that you do not attribute to Allah [due] grandeur

71:14.en: While He has created you in stages

71:15.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ ا
71:15.en: Do you not consider how Allah has created seven heavens in layers

71:16.ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجࣰ ا
71:16.en: And made the moon therein a [reflected] light and made the sun a burning lamp

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a [progressive] growth

71:18.ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجࣰ ا
71:18.en: Then He will return you into it and extract you [another] extraction

71:19.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطࣰ ا
71:19.en: And Allah has made for you the earth an expanse

71:20.ar: لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡهَا سُبُلࣰ ا فِجَاجࣰ ا
71:20.en: That you may follow therein roads of passage

36:11.ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَخَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِمَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَأَجۡرࣲ كَرِيمٍ
36:11.en: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided

26:109.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:109.en: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: So the eminent among those who disbelieved from his people said, "We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion. And we do not see in you over us any merit; rather, we think you are liars

11:29.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
11:29.en: And O my people, I ask not of you for it any wealth. My reward is not but from Allah. And I am not one to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly

11:36.ar: وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
11:36.en: And it was revealed to Noah that, "No one will believe from your people except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: And construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned

W5FbJZsVtHw.title: Surat Nuh Part 1: Verses 1-9
W5FbJZsVtHw.one_line: Nuh rehearsing his defence before Allah: commitment of time and variety of methods in dawah, and what Muslim communities lack in both.
W5FbJZsVtHw.summary: He opens the second half of the 29th juz, where the surahs move from representing Islam for oneself to representing it for others. Most dawah, he argues, happens through character; preaching only reaches people already searching, so the first four surahs of the cluster had to come first. Surat Nuh then shows a prophet who did everything right and still saw few results, contrasting with the jinn who accepted without being addressed. He asks the audience to imagine standing behind Nuh on the Day of Judgment and hearing him prepare his argument for why only a handful believed. Nuh's case has three parts. First, time: he called his people night and day without pause. Second, motive: he sought only their forgiveness, which leads to a warning that dawah can never be transactional. Third, method: he spoke publicly, in gatherings, and privately. Along the way he explains why warnings come before glad tidings, why the appointed term cannot be delayed, and why Nuh's people's arrogance and contempt for the poor blocked them. He applies each point to today: the community's deepest gap is committed volunteers rather than ideas, and its outreach lacks creativity even though simple methods work. He asks people to prioritise service and to try new ways of reaching people.

outline.heading: Dawah happens mostly through character
outline.gist: Verbal preaching is a small part of dawah and only reaches people already searching. What drew people in the Prophet's time was the ethics of the Medinan community.

outline.heading: Representing Islam for yourself before others
outline.gist: The first four surahs of the cluster set the requirements of knowledge, ethics, spirituality and conduct; a preacher who does not practise causes great harm when exposed. Nuh and the jinn will give two contrasting examples.

outline.heading: Memorise half a page a week
outline.gist: These surahs should be known by heart; reciting the weekly half page daily is enough to memorise it.

outline.heading: A Meccan surah and the length of the madd
outline.gist: All surahs of this juz are Meccan and foundational. Most madd are four counts, some six, and their length is relative to recitation speed.

outline.heading: Nuh sent to his own people
outline.gist: The surah is named after Nuh because his life is the example of dawah outcomes; he was sent to his own people, not all of humanity.

outline.heading: Why prophets warn first
outline.gist: Failing to mention what can ruin someone is unforgivable while forgetting a pleasant surprise is not; the Quran still always pairs warning with reward.

outline.heading: Worship, taqwa and obedience sum up the deen
outline.gist: Serve Allah, be mindful of Him and follow the messenger: a mindset of service, a system of self-protection, and adherence to teachings.

outline.heading: Tajweed: keeping the ra distinct before the lam
outline.gist: The lam can merge into the ra but not the reverse, a common mistake in yaghfir lakum.

outline.heading: Forgiveness and deferral to an appointed term
outline.gist: Forgiveness reaches the sins themselves and punishment is postponed, but no one escapes death; when Allah's set term comes nothing delays it.

outline.heading: A physician's experience of prognosis
outline.gist: Doctors are wrong about life expectancy more often than right; patients outlive predictions or die suddenly, so live well now.

outline.heading: Standing behind Nuh as he rehearses his case
outline.gist: If one of the mightiest prophets prepares his argument before Allah, we should be worried about our own.

outline.heading: 950 years and a handful of believers
outline.gist: Even the highest count of his followers is 73, and his own wife and son refused, so he must explain why the outcome was not achieved.

outline.heading: Answering for a job not done
outline.gist: An employer asks why the job failed; in Allah's court the questions are just, but Nuh still has to account.

outline.heading: We are not better than Nuh
outline.gist: Nuh's mostly verbal dawah failed while the Prophet's unspoken conduct moved the jinn; guidance is Allah's, but each of us must make Nuh's argument.

outline.heading: First argument: called them night and day
outline.gist: Nuh shows he gave all his time; prophets had no holidays, and their rest was only what the body required.

outline.heading: Consistency that only drove them away
outline.gist: His persistence only increased their flight. He outlines the three things he must prove: time, method and substance.

outline.heading: No agenda but their forgiveness
outline.gist: Every call was so Allah would forgive them; prophets disown any hidden aim, and suspicion of preachers is a healthy instinct.

outline.heading: Dawah cannot be transactional
outline.gist: Guidance has no price tag; neither the teacher expecting compensation nor the payer feeling entitled is on the right road, which makes paid imam roles difficult.

outline.heading: Fingers in ears and covered faces
outline.gist: Istaghshaw means deliberately wrapping themselves in their garments, and the doubled form istakbaru istikbara stresses open, declared arrogance.

outline.heading: Contempt for Nuh's poor followers
outline.gist: Nuh's people despised the poor who followed him, as other surahs show, and he refused to drive them away.

outline.heading: Commitment: the community's biggest gap
outline.gist: Few people champion any cause; most come with expectations. Volunteer-based Islamic work needs people who give fixed time and money regardless of convenience.

outline.heading: Ideas without anyone to do the work
outline.gist: Communities have endless ideas and a handful of people carrying the unglamorous work.

outline.heading: Say it was not a priority, not that you were busy
outline.gist: Everyone is busy; missing a commitment means it did not make your list, and you should hear yourself say so.

outline.heading: Gaza advocacy fizzled while Nuh never quit
outline.gist: Daily protests after October 2023 faded because opponents wait out short-lived passion; Nuh kept going until Allah told him to stop and build the ark.

outline.heading: Night before day: total consistency
outline.gist: Other faith groups have far more committed volunteers. Nuh mentions night first to show no hour was spared.

outline.heading: Commitment fits your stage of life
outline.gist: A young person's commitment is seeking knowledge; people who drift in and out of the masjid like tides cannot build anything, whatever the Eid numbers.

outline.heading: Second argument: public, gatherings and private
outline.gist: Nuh called openly, addressed groups and spoke one-on-one in confidence. He notes the difference between asrartu and asrartu with a different letter.

outline.heading: People need different settings
outline.gist: Like a shopper who wants to browse alone, some want a general talk, some a group setting, some a private conversation; all three must be offered.

outline.heading: Nuh used every method he had; we have far more
outline.gist: Without phones or print, Nuh went to people's homes; today there are written, online and programme methods, yet Muslims lack creativity.

outline.heading: Simple ways to bring people in
outline.gist: Sports nights for young men and women and free food draw people easily, but only committed mentors turn attendance into guidance.

outline.heading: What masajid are for
outline.gist: Many masajid are run by people who do not know their purpose: Allah's house exists to welcome, mentor, teach and support.

outline.heading: Drop methods that no longer work
outline.gist: If a method fails for years, stop; door-to-door preaching, as Jehovah's Witnesses practise it, no longer suits people.

outline.heading: Third argument: the substance of the message
outline.gist: Having proved time and method, Nuh will show his message itself was sound, a narrative he finds remarkably scientific, to be read in the next session.

themes.note: Nuh's argument is the model for accounting for dawah: time, motive and method.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Even Nuh must explain why the outcome was not reached; we must be ready to make the same case.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Lack of committed volunteers is the community's main challenge; busy is not an excuse but a statement of priorities.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Dawah must carry no hidden agenda or expectation of compensation.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: The appointed term cannot be delayed; even physicians cannot predict it.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette
themes.note: Masajid should welcome and mentor through creative programmes and drop methods that fail.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Advocacy for Gaza faded with time, showing passion without commitment.

2:196.ar: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذࣰ ى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةࣱ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكࣲۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامࣲ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةࣱ كَامِلَةࣱۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
2:196.en: And complete the Hajj and 'umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned [home]. Those are ten complete [days]. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty

2:203.ar: ۞وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيٓ أَيَّامࣲ مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۖ لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
2:203.en: And remember Allah during [specific] numbered days. Then whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays [until the third] - there is no sin upon him - for him who fears Allah. And fear Allah and know that unto Him you will be gathered

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein [by entering the state of ihram], there is [to be for him] no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do - Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding

5:96.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ صَيۡدُ ٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَطَعَامُهُۥ مَتَٰعࣰ ا لَّكُمۡ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِۖ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ صَيۡدُ ٱلۡبَرِّ مَا دُمۡتُمۡ حُرُمࣰ اۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
5:96.en: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah to whom you will be gathered

22:28.ar: لِّيَشۡهَدُواْ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمۡ وَيَذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ فِيٓ أَيَّامࣲ مَّعۡلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِۖ فَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا وَأَطۡعِمُواْ ٱلۡبَآئِسَ ٱلۡفَقِيرَ
22:28.en: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor

22:29.ar: ثُمَّ لۡيَقۡضُواْ تَفَثَهُمۡ وَلۡيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمۡ وَلۡيَطَّوَّفُواْ بِٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ
22:29.en: Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the ancient House

YXwJ3T6ltjE.title: The Fiqh of Hajj
YXwJ3T6ltjE.one_line: A practical guide to Hajj rulings: pillars, obligations, sunnahs, prohibitions, miqats and the sites, choosing the easiest sound views.
YXwJ3T6ltjE.summary: He explains that the Prophet's Hajj corrected rites corrupted by pre-Islamic Arabs, which is why he answered so many questions with 'do it, no harm'. Since following one madhhab is nearly impossible amid three million pilgrims, he teaches the easiest sound views while taking precautions on pillars: know the pillars and what invalidates Hajj, follow your group in the rest, and offer a sacrifice when unsure. The four pillars are ihram, Arafah, tawaf al-ifadah and sa'y; a missed pillar must be performed, while a missed obligation is made up by a sacrifice. He goes through seven obligations: ihram from the miqat, standing at Arafah until sunset, Muzdalifah, nights at Mina, stoning in order, shaving, and farewell tawaf, which he considers sunnah; those unable to sacrifice fast ten days. Sunnahs include bathing and perfuming the body, talbiyah, idtiba', raml, two rak'at near the Maqam, hastening between the green lights, Zamzam and touching the Black Stone, and missing them costs nothing. He covers ihram dress for men and women, the miqats, and the three prohibitions of intimacy, sin and argument, warning that a marriage contract in Hajj is void and patience will be tested. He closes with the layout of the Ka'bah, the mas'a, Arafah's boundaries and the jamarat.

outline.heading: The Prophet's Hajj corrected corrupted rites
outline.gist: Pagan Arabs had mixed idolatrous practices into Ibrahim's Hajj, so people watched the Prophet to know what to keep and drop.

outline.heading: 'Do it, there is no harm'
outline.gist: Surrounded by questions, the Prophet often answered with leniency about order and timing.

outline.heading: Do not insist on one madhhab in Hajj
outline.gist: With up to three million people in a small area, rigid adherence can endanger lives; learn a text, then follow your group's guide.

outline.heading: His approach: easiest sound views, and a sacrifice when unsure
outline.gist: He picks the easiest positions across madhhabs; many scholars advise offering a sacrifice anyway since no pilgrim is free of shortcomings.

outline.heading: Being prevented from Hajj (2:196)
outline.gist: One prevented after ihram sacrifices where he can, and must not shave before the sacrifice.

outline.heading: The four pillars
outline.gist: Ihram, tawaf, sa'y and Arafah; the Hanafis count only ihram and Arafah, the easiest view.

outline.heading: Pillar versus obligation
outline.gist: As with prayer, a missed pillar must be performed and cannot be replaced by a sacrifice.

outline.heading: The pilgrim who never performed tawaf
outline.gist: Only tawaf al-ifadah is a pillar; a brother who skipped tawaf entirely was told to fly back, until a Hanafi scholar eased it.

outline.heading: Tawaf and sa'y may be delayed
outline.gist: Someone who left for Madinah without sa'y must return in ihram; these two can be done late with a sacrifice.

outline.heading: Ihram and Arafah are bound to time
outline.gist: Ihram must come before the other pillars; forgetting it means losing the Hajj.

outline.heading: The time of Arafah: 'Hajj is Arafah'
outline.gist: Standing runs from fajr of the ninth to fajr of Eid; standing only at night is valid with a sacrifice; missing the day loses Hajj.

outline.heading: One sacrifice or several
outline.gist: Mistakes of the same kind need one sacrifice; different kinds may need more, so ask; Saudi guides now teach several madhhabs.

outline.heading: Umrah: the same minus Arafah
outline.gist: Its pillars are ihram, tawaf and sa'y.

outline.heading: Know the pillars and what invalidates Hajj
outline.gist: Every other act is an obligation, a sunnah or a prohibition; get the pillars right, avoid invalidators, follow people and offer a sacrifice.

outline.heading: Interlude
Obligation one: ihram from the miqat
outline.gist: Ihram is a pillar but its place is an obligation; ihram after the miqat or from Makkah in tamattu' requires a sacrifice.

outline.heading: Obligation two: Arafah by day until sunset
outline.gist: Arriving after sunset is valid with a sacrifice; several shortfalls of the same kind need only one.

outline.heading: Obligation three: Muzdalifah
outline.gist: Spending the night until midnight is obligatory on the precautionary view; the aim is caution without hardship.

outline.heading: Obligation four: nights at Mina
outline.gist: Two nights are obligatory, the third sunnah; he explains the day of tarwiyah, when pilgrims filled their waterskins, and the days of tashreeq.

outline.heading: Obligation five: stoning in order
outline.gist: Unlike prayer, deliberately skipping an obligation does not void Hajj but requires a sacrifice.

outline.heading: Obligation six: shaving or trimming
outline.gist: Some count it a pillar; he treats it as an obligation that releases from ihram.

outline.heading: Obligation seven: farewell tawaf
outline.gist: There is one tawaf pillar; arrival and farewell tawaf are extra, and he holds farewell tawaf to be sunnah.

outline.heading: Fasting ten days if unable to sacrifice
outline.gist: Three days in Hajj and seven at home; earlier scholars advised sacrificing and also fasting as a precaution.

outline.heading: Hajj once in a lifetime, done carefully
outline.gist: Once cheap and repeated often, Hajj is now costly and crowded; doing it more than once takes another's place.

outline.heading: Sunnah: bathing and perfuming the body
outline.gist: Perfume the body, not the garment; leave makeup and adornment at home, since cologne after ihram costs a sheep; hardship returns you to your origin.

outline.heading: Sunnah: talbiyah
outline.gist: Men raise their voices, women lower theirs unless among women.

outline.heading: Sunnah: tawaf of arrival
outline.gist: Any tawaf done after Arafah counts for the pillar tawaf.

outline.heading: Sunnah: idtiba'
outline.gist: Men bare the right shoulder, from the Prophet's umrah when Quraysh claimed the Muslims were weak.

outline.heading: Sunnah: raml
outline.gist: A brisk military jog in the first three circuits, usually impossible in today's crowds.

outline.heading: Sunnah: two rak'at at the Maqam
outline.gist: Do not push people; intend them at the Maqam and pray anywhere in the Haram.

outline.heading: Sunnahs of sa'y
outline.gist: Seven legs from Safa to Marwa, hastening between the green lights as Hajar did, facing the Ka'bah to say takbir and make dua at each hill.

outline.heading: Zamzam and the Black Stone
outline.gist: Drink Zamzam with dua; intending to touch the Black Stone suffices when it cannot be reached.

outline.heading: Missing a sunnah costs nothing
outline.gist: No sacrifice or penalty for sunnahs; know the pillars and obligations well.

outline.heading: Men's ihram: no sewn garments
outline.gist: Sewn means pieces stitched into a shape; ihram is a single piece of cloth.

outline.heading: Women in ihram
outline.gist: Women wear normal modest clothing but do not cover face or hands; group colours are fine; each spouse owes their own sacrifice, with no family discount.

outline.heading: The meaning of miqat and the five miqats
outline.gist: Miqat joins a time and a place; Dhul-Hulayfah, al-Juhfah, Dhat Irq, Qarn al-Manazil and Yalamlam surround Makkah at different distances.

outline.heading: Miqat lines and ihram from inside the Haram
outline.gist: The miqat is a line parallel to these points; for another umrah step outside the Haram boundary; ihram once lasted up to two weeks.

outline.heading: No intimacy: rafath
outline.gist: Intercourse invalidates Hajj on the stronger view and requires another Hajj; it still happens every year now that Mina has hotels.

outline.heading: A marriage contract in Hajj is void
outline.gist: Even with dowry and paperwork, such a contract is invalid; agree to talk after Hajj.

outline.heading: No sin: fusuq
outline.gist: Sins and the prohibition on hunting while in ihram.

outline.heading: No argument: jidal
outline.gist: Among millions your patience will be tested; if you lose your temper, offer a sacrifice and walk away from quarrels.

outline.heading: Idle talk versus beneficial speech
outline.gist: Following football during tawaf is idle talk; talk of rites, lessons and even trade is allowed (22:28).

outline.heading: The talbiyah and when to stop it
outline.gist: The Prophet's wording and other authentic forms; stop on reaching the Haram or Arafah.

outline.heading: 'Take your rites from me'
outline.gist: The companions raised their voices until hoarse; the Prophet unified tribes' differing rituals.

outline.heading: Flexible timings: tawaf al-ifadah and stoning
outline.gist: The old dispute on stoning before or after noon has no benefit today; stone any time and on behalf of the elderly.

outline.heading: Starting tawaf
outline.gist: Begin at the Black Stone line with the Ka'bah on your left, saying takbir.

outline.heading: Hijr Isma'il is part of the Ka'bah
outline.gist: The Prophet left it outside to avoid alarming new Muslims; voluntary prayer there counts as inside the Ka'bah, obligatory prayer does not.

outline.heading: The four corners
outline.gist: The Yemeni, Iraqi and Shami corners face their regions.

outline.heading: The Multazam and the Maqam
outline.gist: The Prophet pressed his chest to the wall between the door and the Black Stone in dua; pray tawaf rak'at anywhere if the Maqam is crowded.

outline.heading: Floors of the mas'a and wheelchairs
outline.gist: Tawaf and sa'y on upper floors are valid; the tired may be pushed.

outline.heading: Dua in sa'y and tawaf
outline.gist: No fixed words are required; recite Quran and make any dua.

outline.heading: Resist the urge to complain
outline.gist: Sore feet bring out the devil of complaining; keep your tongue to good.

outline.heading: Wudu for tawaf and sa'y
outline.gist: The majority require wudu for tawaf, Abu Hanifah does not, and one may follow him; for sa'y it is sunnah.

outline.heading: Know the boundaries of Arafah
outline.gist: One pilgrim spent the whole day outside Arafah without realizing; ask rather than follow the crowd.

outline.heading: Distances between the sites
outline.gist: Arafah to Mina is about 14 km, Mina to the Haram about 8 km; plan before walking.

outline.heading: Stoning: order and the seventy pebbles
outline.gist: Aqabah on Eid, then all three in order on each day of tashreeq, seventy pebbles in total; stoning for the weak is allowed.

outline.heading: Outro
